newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon FTML signs $100 mln loan with IFC, banks.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon FTML signs $100 mln loan with IFC, banks.

text.p: France Telecom Mobile Liban signed on Wednesday a $100 million syndicated loan with the World Bank, the group Societe Generale and a number of local banks to expand its cellular network in Lebanon.
The six-year loan carries an interest rate of six months LIBOR plus three percentage points.
FTML, which has a capital of $30 million, made $13 million net profit in 1996 and was expected to make $16 million to $17 million in 1997, FTML Chairman Salah Bouraad told a news conference.

"Since the self-financing capacity of the company has not yet reached its investments volume, we are signing today the loan approval with the International Finance Corporation, the group SG and the other participating banks," Bouraad said.
Representative of the IFC -- the private sector arm of the World Bank -- Mohsen Khalil said the FTML provided a model for the role of the private sector in activating the economy.
"This is why the IFC decided to take part in the deal which grants FTML the loan without any guarantees whether from the government or from shareholders," he said.
Chairman Maurice Sehnaoui of the Societe Generale Libano Europeenne de Banque, the local arranger of the deal, said the operation provided a model for project finance in Lebanon.

"This operation is model as it provides a balance between local and international financing. It will reflect positively on Lebanon's balance of payments and add value to the sector which will eventually go back to the public sector," he said.
Nineteen local and international banks participated in the loan.

Cellis, the name under which FTML has been operating its service in Lebanon since 1994, has a 10-year build, operate and transfer (BOT) deal with the Lebanese government. It is renewable in 2004 for two years.
Cellis has 137,000 subscribers who use the cellular at a record average of 750 minutes per subscriber per month compared with a world average of 130 minutes per month.
It will use the loan to help finance its $190 million plan to expand the cellular phone network while maximising the quality of service over a period of less than five years.

"To compensate for irregular absence of channels free of all interference, FTML is proceeding with its investments for the development of its network, and particulary in the densification of the Greater Beirut area," Bouraad said.
The densification process consists of reducing the size of the cells to increase the reuse of one same group of frequencies on different cells, he said.

"We will continue this densification that we started in 1996 as a remedy to the congestion or the saturation of the network at peak times, mainly due to the interference and the excessive use of the network by the subscribers," he added.
